title: Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims: Invoice Value of the Containers a Cover Takes
content:
The commercial invoice value on which a cover of `Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims` is bound is spread across the containers of the booking, and the cover takes its proportion of it.

## Definition

To find the invoice value of the goods a cover takes, begin with the declared cargo value appearing on the holder's transport document for the booking the cover protects. Multiply it by the containers the cover takes, divide by the containers that booking carries in the holder's booking record, and round to the cent.

If one of the two records is absent or empty, the quoted insured value stays unchanged.

## Input, judgement, output (hypothetical figures)

| Declared cargo value on the transport document (USD) | Containers on the booking | Containers the cover takes | Value quoted (USD) | Value for binding (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 250000.00 | 5 | 5 | 230000.00 | 250000.00 |
| 250000.00 | 5 | 3 | 140000.00 | 150000.00 |
| 100000.00 | 3 | 2 | 60000.00 | 66666.67 |
| none on record | 5 | 3 | 140000.00 | 140000.00 |

In the third row, 100000.00 multiplied by 2 and divided by 3 is 66666.666, which rounds to 66666.67.
